title: Inject a service with lifetimes
summary: Replace a hidden construction with constructor injection and choose service lifetimes.

scenario.briefing: OrderService creates its own clock, so tests cannot control time. Register the clock in the container, inject it through the constructor, and keep request state scoped.

objectives.description: Resolve the clock through constructor injection.
Choose a lifetime for a request-bound repository.
Explain lifetimes and captive dependencies accurately.

hints: The service currently calls new SystemClock().
Add an IClock parameter to the constructor.
Register IClock and SystemClock with AddSingleton.
Resolve OrderService from the provider instead of constructing it.

misconceptions.description: Constructing the dependency inside the service.
misconceptions.testDescription: The clock is resolved from the container.
misconceptions.feedback: A hidden new makes the dependency impossible to replace in a test. Accept IClock through the constructor.

misconceptions.description: Registering a request-bound repository as a singleton.
misconceptions.feedback: A repository that holds a request-scoped DbContext must be scoped as well. A singleton would capture it for the process lifetime.

misconceptions.description: Sharing a DbContext as a singleton.
misconceptions.feedback: DbContext is not thread-safe and is designed for a short scope. Register it scoped and resolve it per request.

sections.title: Constructor injection makes dependencies explicit
sections.body: A class that receives its dependencies through its constructor can be constructed with real or test implementations. It does not create hidden collaborators with new. The container builds the object graph and supplies each dependency.

sections.title: Lifetimes describe sharing
sections.body: A singleton is created once per container and shared. A scoped service is created once per request scope. A transient service is created for every resolution. The lifetime must match the state the service holds; a singleton that captures a scoped DbContext is a captive dependency.

sections.title: Registrations are code
sections.body: IServiceCollection registrations are ordinary code that can be tested. Build the provider once at startup and resolve request-scoped services from a request scope. Do not resolve scoped services from the root provider in a long-running application.
